related_questions.question: Is the American Academy of CPR and First Aid legit?

text_blocks.snippet: The American Academy of CPR and First Aid is a legitimate online provider of CPR and first aid certifications. They are accredited by the Postgraduate Institute for Medicine, which is jointly accredited by the Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education (ACCME). Their certifications are recognized by many employers and meet the standards of the Emergency Cardiovascular Care (ECC) and OSHA.
snippet_highlighted_words: a legitimate online provider of CPR and first aid certifications

list.title: Accreditation:
list.snippet: The American Academy of CPR and First Aid is accredited by a reputable organization in the medical education field, the Postgraduate Institute for Medicine.

list.title: Joint Accreditation:
list.snippet: The Postgraduate Institute for Medicine is jointly accredited by the ACCME, ACPE, and the ANCC, demonstrating a high standard of quality.

list.title: Meeting Standards:
list.snippet: Their certifications align with the standards of the ECC and OSHA, which are important for many workplaces.

list.title: Focus on Education:
list.snippet: The American Academy of CPR and First Aid emphasizes high-quality education and provides CME credits for their courses.

list.title: Online and Blended Options:
list.snippet: They offer both online and blended (online plus hands-on skills) training options, allowing flexibility for learners.

list.title: Card Verification:
list.snippet: They provide a service to verify the authenticity of their certifications, which is useful for employers or others who need to confirm someone's training.

list.title: Review and Feedback:
list.snippet: The organization has received positive reviews for its course design, ease of understanding, and customer service according to reviews on cpraedcourse.com.

list.title: Employer Requirements:
list.snippet: While the American Academy of CPR and First Aid is a legitimate provider, some employers, particularly in healthcare, may prefer certifications from the American Heart Association or the American Red Cross.

list.title: Online vs. In-Person:
list.snippet: Some employers may require in-person skills testing for CPR certification, even if the knowledge portion is completed online.

list.title: Check with Employer:
list.snippet: It's always a good idea to confirm with your employer about their specific requirements for CPR and first aid certification before signing up for a course.
